what_happened: In job 2rep, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The job concerns per-role model and effort settings and escalation for hard jobs. The first reading put the hard-job escalation in the planner and critic stages. Job planning has been switched off (f80b05a), so those roles never run. The user redirected it. Explicit model and effort per role stay in config and on every invocation record. The escalation moves to the producer: a reading that judges a job hard (for example one changing landing, the history check or records) picks a stronger model or higher effort and records the reason. Ordinary jobs keep the default. The user also asked athena status to show first-pass verification rate, landed share and cost per landed job by producer model and effort.
cause: The reading is built from the request text and is not checked against the live athena.toml. Nothing tells the reading stage which pipeline roles are enabled, so a feature can be assigned to a role that a config switch such as [job_plan] enabled = false has turned off. Only the user knows the current state. The same correction came back one case earlier, in qy2p, where the reading also targeted the planner and critic. A fix there did not carry over to other jobs.
prevention: Give the reading stage the list of enabled and disabled pipeline roles from the current athena.toml. Add a code check at reading acceptance. It scans the reading's deliverables and criteria for roles that are disabled in config and rejects the reading, naming each role and the enabled roles that could take the work. A reading that targets a disabled role would then be sent back before the user sees it. The same applies to any later job that touches planner, critic or other switchable roles.
proposed_request: Make the per-role model and effort settings and the hard-job escalation work with job planning switched off (athena.toml [job_plan] enabled = false). Outcomes: (1) Every role keeps an explicit model and effort in config, and every invocation record shows the model and effort used. (2) The escalation applies to the producer only. When the reading judges a job hard, for example one that changes landing, the history check or records, the producer runs with a stronger model or higher effort, and the reason is recorded on the job. An ordinary job uses the default producer model and effort. (3) athena status shows first-pass verification rate, landed share and cost per landed job, grouped by producer model and effort. Do not add escalation logic to the planner or critic briefs or code, since those roles do not run. Acceptance: tests show a hard-job reading selects the stronger producer setting and records the reason; an ordinary job keeps the default; invocation records carry model and effort for all roles; athena status prints the three measures per producer model and effort, including an empty case with no jobs; the existing budgets and config tests still pass.
